<r>Ant.</r> Prope est iam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est iam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est iam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est iam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Continuation of the Holy Gospel according to Luke
<r>Luke 3:1-6</r>
<c>I</c>n the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea. And so on.

Homily by Pope St. Gregory <n>the Great.</n>
<r>10th on the Gospels.</r>
<c>T</c>he date, at which the Fore-runner of our Redeemer entered on his public office of preaching, is indicated to us by the name of the ruler of the Roman Commonwealth, and by those of the princes of Palestine. The time of his preaching is indicated by these names, because he came as the Fore-runner of Him Who was to be the Redeemer of some Jews and many Gentiles. Moreover in the enumeration of these worldly monarchs there is a foreshadowing of the fact, that the Gentiles were about to be gathered into one, and the Jews to be scattered abroad in punishment of their unbelief; in the whole heathen Commonwealth we find the title of one Emperor, but in the small kingdom of Judaea are mentioned four masters.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Send forth the Lamb, O Lord, the Ruler of the land; from the rock in the wilderness unto the mount of the daughter of Zion.
<r>℣.</r> Ex Sion spécies decóris ejus: Deus noster véniet.
* From the rock in the wilderness unto the mount of the daughter of Zion.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<c>Q</c>uia autem gentílitas colligénda erat, et Iudǽa pro culpa perfídiæ dispergénda, ipsa quoque descríptio terréni principátus osténdit: quóniam et in Romána república unus præfuísse descríbitur, et in Iudǽæ regno per quartam partem plúrimi principabántur. Voce étenim nostri Redemptóris dícitur: Omne regnum in seípsum divisum desolábitur. Liquet ergo, quod ad finem regni Iudǽa pervénerat, quæ tot régibus divísa subiacébat.

<h>Reading 2</h>
Continuation of the Holy Gospel according to Luke
<r>Luke 3:1-6</r>
<c>I</c>n the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea. And so on.

Homily by Pope St. Gregory <n>the Great.</n>
<r>10th on the Gospels.</r>
<c>T</c>he date, at which the Fore-runner of our Redeemer entered on his public office of preaching, is indicated to us by the name of the ruler of the Roman Commonwealth, and by those of the princes of Palestine. The time of his preaching is indicated by these names, because he came as the Fore-runner of Him Who was to be the Redeemer of some Jews and many Gentiles. Moreover in the enumeration of these worldly monarchs there is a foreshadowing of the fact, that the Gentiles were about to be gathered into one, and the Jews to be scattered abroad in punishment of their unbelief; in the whole heathen Commonwealth we find the title of one Emperor, but in the small kingdom of Judaea are mentioned four masters. The blessed voice of the Saviour itself hath said, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation <n>Luke xi. 17.</n> And we may well look for the ruin of the Jewish state when we see it divided among so many rulers. We observe likewise that the names of the reigning priests as well as kings are given. The Evangelist Luke hath left on record the chiefs both of the monarchy and of the priesthood who held office when John the Baptist began to preach, because John preached Him Who is at once our Priest and our King.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> The waste places have brought forth sweet-smelling buds for Israel; for, behold, our God will come with power.
* And His brightness is with Him.
<r>℣.</r> Ecce dominátor Dóminus cum virtúte véniet.
<r>℟.</r> And His brightness is with Him.

b.ddef32ad3c:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>T</c>ertiodécimo Kaléndas Ianuárii Luna undécima. Anno Dómini 2026
<h>V</h>igília sancti Thomæ Apóstoli.
<h>R</h>omæ natális sancti Zephyríni, Papæ et Mártyris. Ipsíus tamen festum recólitur séptimo Kaléndas Septémbris.
<h>I</h>bídem pássio sancti Ignátii, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, tértius post beátum Petrum Apóstolum, Antiochénam rexit Ecclésiam. Hic, in persecutióne Traiáni, damnátus ad béstias, Romam vinctus míttitur; ibíque, circumsedénte Senátu, immaníssimis pœnárum supplíciis primo est afféctus, dehinc obiícitur leónibus, quorum déntibus præfocátus, hóstia Christi effícitur. Eius vero festívitas Kaléndis Februárii celebrátur.
<h>I</h>tem Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Liberáti et Báiuli.
<h>I</h>n Arábia sanctórum Mártyrum Eugénii et Macárii Presbyterórum, qui a Iuliáno Apóstata, cum ipsíus impietátem arguíssent, sævíssimis plagis affécti sunt, atque in vastíssimam erémum relegáti, et gládio cæsi.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ sanctórum mílitum et Mártyrum Ammónis, Zenónis, Ptolemǽi, Ingenis et Theóphili; qui, tribunálibus astántes, cum quidam Christiánus, in supplíciis pósitus, trepidáret et iam prope ad negándum declináret, vultu, óculis ac nútibus illum conabántur erígere. Cumque hac de causa clamor totíus pópuli in eos prosilíret, prorumpéntes in médium se Christiános esse testáti sunt; per quorum victóriam Christus, qui suis eam animi constántiam déderat, gloriosíssime triumphávit.
<h>G</h>éldubæ, in Germánia, sancti Iúlii Mártyris.

<h>B</h>ríxiæ sancti Domínici, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>I</h>n Hispánia deposítio sancti Domínici de Sylos Abbátis, e sancti Benedícti Ordine, miráculis in captivórum liberatióne celebérrimi.

b.f29d498d8e:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>D</c>ecember 20th 2026, the 11th day of the Moon,
<h>T</h>omorrow is the eve of the holy Apostle Thomas.
<h>U</h>pon the same 20th day of December, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, [in the year 219,] the holy Pope and martyr Zephyrinus, whose feast, however, is kept upon the 26th day of August.
<h>L</h>ikewise at Rome, the passion of the holy Bishop and martyr Ignatius, who ruled the church of Antioch as the third Bishop of that See in succession to the blessed Apostle Peter. In the persecution under the Emperor Trajan he was condemned to be killed by wild beasts, and was sent to Rome in chains. There, in the presence of the Senate, he was first put to most grievous torments and then thrown to lions, the which throttled him with their teeth, and so he was made Christ's offering, (in the year 107.) His feast, however, is kept upon the 1st day of February.
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyrs Liberatus and Bajulus.
<h>I</h>n Arabia, the holy martyrs Eugenius and Macarius, two Priests who blamed the ungodliness of the Emperor Julian the Apostate, and for that cause were most cruelly flogged and sent out into the great desert, where they were slain with the sword, (in the year 362.)
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, the holy soldiers and martyrs Ammon, Zeno, Ptolemy, Ingenes, and Theophilus. They were on guard beside the judgment-seat when a certain Christian who was under the torture began to waver and was almost giving way, and they tried by signs to encourage him to hold out; for this cause all the people cried out against them, and they came forward and confessed themselves to be Christians and Christ, who Himself had given such steadfastness unto His own, did Himself most gloriously triumph in their victory, (in the year 249.)
<h>A</h>t Geldube, (in Thrace,) the holy martyr Julius, (fourth century.)
<h>A</h>t Antioch, holy Philogonius, Patriarch of the see. He was an advocate when he was called by the will of God to govern that church, and first took up the contending for the Catholic faith along with holy Bishop Alexander, and his Companions, against Arius. He fell asleep in the Lord, illustrious for good works, (in the year 322.) Holy John Chrysostom preached an eloquent sermon on his feast-day.
<h>A</h>t Brescia, the holy Confessor Dominic, Bishop (of that see, about the year 612.)
<h>O</h>n this day is commemorated the burial in Spain of holy Dominic, Abbot of Silos, (in the diocese of Burgos, in Castile, which abbey he founded,) of the Order of St. Benedict, very famous for his miracles wrought for the liberation of captives. (He died in his monastery at Silos, on December 14, 1073.)
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.b5906d2c79:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>S</c>tir up, we beseech thee, O Lord, thy power, and come; make haste to our aid with thy great might; that, by the help of thy grace, that which is hindered by our sins may be hastened by thy merciful forgiveness.
<h>W</h>ho livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.042c2247e8:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui cónspicis, quia ex nostra pravitáte afflígimur: concéde propítius; ut ex tua visitatióne consolémur:
<h>Q</h>ui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.303541cf4d:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Who seest that by reason of our sins we are sorely afflicted, mercifully grant unto us by thy visitation effectually to be comforted.
<h>W</h>ho livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.274e44e365:
<h>Regula vel Evangelium</h>
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
Reguláribus disciplínis instruat nos Magíster caléstis.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>D</c>onet Dóminus ut observétis hæc ómnia, tamquam spirituális pulchritúdinis amatóres; et bono Christi odóre de bona vestra conversatióne fragrántes: non sicut servi sub lege, sed sicut líberi sub grátia constitúti.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
Commemorátio Fratrum, Sorórum, Familiárium, Benefactórum defunctórum Ordinis nostri.
Requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Psalmus 116</r>
§11.66d6af014b
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Osténde nobis, Dómine, misericórdiam tuam.
<r>℟.</r> Et salutáre tuum da nobis.

<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>A</c>ctiónes nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, aspirándo prǽveni et adiuvándo proséquere: ut cuncta nostra orátio et operátio a te semper incípiat, et per te cœpta finiátur.
Per Christum Dóminum nostrum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Adiutórium nostrum ✠ in nómine Dómini.
<r>℟.</r> Qui fecit cælum et terram.
<n>Si non sequitur aliqua Hora dicitur</n>
<r>℣.</r> Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.71da482b7a:
<h>Regula vel Evangelium</h>
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
May the heavenly Master instruct us in the discipline of the Rule.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>M</c>ay the Lord grant that you observe all these things as lovers of spiritual beauty, and giving forth the good odour of Christ by your good life: not as servants under the law, but as free men established under grace.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
Commemoration of the deceased Brethren, Sisters, Relations and Benefactors of our Order.
Requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Psalm 116</r>
§11.0a67a14e81
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Show us, O Lord, thy mercy.
<r>℟.</r> And grant us thy salvation.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>D</c>irect, we beseech thee, O Lord, our actions by thy holy inspiration, and carry them on by thy gracious assistance: that every prayer and work of ours may always begin from thee, and by thee be happily ended.
Through Christ our Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Our help is ✠ in the name of the Lord,
<r>℟.</r> Who made heaven and earth.
<n>Si non sequitur aliqua Hora dicitur</n>
<r>℣.</r> May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
